device_verifications.transport: Sony Digital Paper App loopback relay to USB-connected device
observations: Pagination verified with a page size of 10 across more than 100 entries.
Unicode path resolution succeeded.
PDF download returned ETag and metadata returned file_revision.
No document names, paths, IDs, contents, client IDs, keys, or certificate fingerprints were recorded.

device_verifications.transport: Sony Digital Paper App loopback relay to USB-connected device
observations: Folder creation, document copy, document rename and move, folder rename, whole-PDF upload, and revision-guarded replacement succeeded.
A deliberately incorrect target_revision was rejected with error_code 40017 and did not change the uploaded test document.
The optional file_hash upload query was omitted because the reference does not specify its algorithm; upload and replacement succeeded without it.
Downloaded SHA-256 values for the device copy and uploaded document matched the approved source PDF.
The approved source document retained its size, revision, and metadata hash; no delete or viewer-open operation was performed.
Test copies were retained in the approved namespace for recovery and inspection; no document names, paths, IDs, client IDs, keys, or certificate fingerprints were recorded.

device_verifications.transport: Sony Digital Paper App loopback relay to USB-connected device
observations: A UUID-named folder tree and UUID-named PDF copy were created specifically for destructive testing; no pre-existing entry was selected as a deletion target.
The CLI refused rmdir while the generated child folder contained the generated PDF.
Document deletion with the resolved current target_revision succeeded and post-delete metadata lookup confirmed absence.
Empty child-folder and top-level test-folder deletion with force_delete_flag false succeeded and post-delete metadata lookup confirmed absence.
The approved source PDF and retained safe-write artifacts were read-only verified after the test and remained present.
mDNS advertised Digital Paper DPT-RP1 on _digitalpaper._tcp.local at digitalpaper.local port 8080 on the USB link.
Existing credentials authenticated directly to HTTPS port 8443 without the Sony application loopback relay.
The direct TLS leaf fingerprint matched the certificate fingerprint observed through the relay.
The temporary direct-test credential copy was owner-only and removed after verification.

device_verifications.transport: direct USB Ethernet via digitalpaper.local:8080 and :8443
observations: The device displayed an eight-digit registration PIN.
A wrong PIN was rejected with HTTP 403 and error_code 40301; cleanup removed the incomplete local profile before a new sequence was started.
A fresh RSA-2048 identity registered successfully and authenticated immediately over the direct API.
After the Sony Digital Paper App was quit, the fresh profile independently authenticated and read device status and the root folder listing.
The existing relay profile and Sony application credentials were not modified; no PIN, client ID, key, certificate fingerprint, or document metadata was recorded.
